actuation: pneumatic actuation (positive air pressure for actuator bending, negative vacuum pressure for jamming)
control_variables: tennis ball drop height (400 mm) and ball diameter (65 mm)
inflation pressure during vibration experiments (45 kPa)
vacuum pressure during impact response testing (-80 kPa)
consistent layer jamming media material and dimensions between proposed and conventional layer jamming comparisons
number of measurement repetitions (10 repetitions for bending and stiffness tests)

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: The soft finger achieves a bending angle of up to 105 degrees at 60 kPa input air pressure with a maximum repeatability error under 8 degrees.
The Cross-Sliding jamming mechanism increases the stiffness of the uninflated finger by nearly 7 times as vacuum increases from 0 kPa to -80 kPa.

As the actuator bending angle increases, the rate of stiffness change from the jamming effect decreases because the actuator's inherent pneumatic stiffness increases sharply and dominates total stiffness.

Direct impact on the soft bending actuator results in a rebound height of 80 mm, approximately 2.5 times lower than direct impact on the variable stiffness unit, showing superior impact absorption and cushioning.

Mounting the variable stiffness structure on the upper surface eliminates contact surface deformation and PVDF sensor signal disturbance during vacuum jamming compared to conventional particle and layer jamming.

At 30 deg/s vibration amplitude, grasping force fluctuation with variable stiffness engaged is approximately 30% (about 2.5 times lower than without jamming), preventing object release, and maintains grasp stability up to 120 deg/s.

Positive inflation pressure to the actuator and vacuum pressure to the jamming structure cannot be applied simultaneously because negative pressure stiffens the jamming unit and resists actuator bending.

experimental_setup: Bending test platform: Soft finger fixed to a holder and pressurized from 0 to 60 kPa in 5 kPa steps via an electromagnetic proportional regulator (vacuum at 0 kPa; 10 trials) to record bending angles.

Variable stiffness test platform: Finger mounted on a holder with a force sensor (ZhiQu Ltd.) on a horizontal sliding mold driven 20 mm in reverse motion at 0, 30, 60, and 90 degree bending angles under 0, -20, -40, -60, and -80 kPa vacuum (10 trials per condition).

Impact response (soft contact) test: High-speed camera recording a 65 mm tennis ball dropped from 400 mm onto the soft actuator surface versus the variable stiffness unit under -80 kPa vacuum to measure rebound height.

Jamming stability test: PVDF piezoelectric sensors attached to contact surfaces of the proposed finger, a conventional particle jamming finger (soybean grains), and a conventional layer jamming finger under vacuum to record surface deformation and signal fluctuations.

Grasping stability vibration test: Three-fingered gripper holding an object on a holder equipped with a flexible force sensor (FS-L-0095-103-ST), vibration motor, and IMU sensor measuring angular velocity amplitudes (~30 deg/s and ~120 deg/s) at 45 kPa inflation pressure with jamming on versus off.

Grasping performance test: Three-fingered gripper performing sequential positive pressure bending, negative pressure stiffening, lifting, and transferring across diverse items (fragile, soft, irregular, and daily objects).
future_work: Addressing anisotropic bending moments caused by the uneven distribution of single versus double jamming media along the Cross-Sliding mechanism.
Applying the Cross-Sliding jamming mechanism to rehabilitation soft robots requiring safe interaction alongside high output forces or high variable stiffness.

bending angle of the finger (0, 30, 60, 90 degrees)
contact surface location (soft bending actuator surface vs. variable stiffness unit surface)
jamming mechanism configuration (proposed Cross-Sliding jamming vs. conventional layer jamming vs. conventional soybean particle jamming)

limitations_inferred: No quantitative mathematical or numerical continuum mechanics models (analytical or finite element) were presented to predict sliding kinematics, contact forces, or stiffness scaling.

The freely suspended midair configuration constrained only by soft limiters and endpoints may pose risks of lateral torsional compliance, misalignment, or frictional wear during repeated high-cycle sliding.
Payload limits were not quantitatively mapped across systematic weight ranges in the reported experiments.
limitations_stated_by_authors: The Cross-Sliding jamming structure has an uneven distribution (single jamming media at the ends, double jamming media at the middle section), causing anisotropic bending moments.
Positive actuation pressure and negative jamming pressure cannot occur simultaneously because negative pressure stiffens the jamming unit and impedes actuator bending.
As the bending angle increases, the rate of stiffness variation due to jamming diminishes because inherent positive-pressure stiffness dominates.
main_results: The soft finger reached a bending angle of up to 105 degrees at 60 kPa input air pressure with repeatability error within 8 degrees.
At 0 degree bending angle, finger stiffness increased by nearly 7-fold as vacuum pressure went from 0 to -80 kPa.
Although total stiffness grew with bending angle, the stiffness variation rate contributed by jamming decreased at higher angles due to dominant inherent pneumatic actuator stiffness.
Soft contact directly with the actuator reduced impact rebound height to 80 mm (approx. 2.5 times lower than rigid contact on the jammed unit), showing superior energy absorption and cushioning.

Relocating the jamming structure to the dorsal surface eliminated contact surface deformation and PVDF signal fluctuations during vacuum application compared to conventional layer and particle jamming.
Under vibration (~30 deg/s and ~120 deg/s), variable stiffness reduced grasping force fluctuation to ~30% (2.5 times less than without jamming) and prevented object slippage/dropping.

A three-fingered gripper successfully grasped and manipulated a diverse variety of soft, fragile, and irregular objects using sequential positive-pressure bending followed by negative-pressure stiffening.
performance_metrics: maximum bending angle (105 degrees at 60 kPa) and repeatability error (<= 8 degrees)
stiffness evaluation index K (slope of displacement-force curve) and stiffness tuning ratio (~7-fold increase at 0 degrees)
impact rebound height (80 mm vs. ~200 mm)
contact surface PVDF sensor fluctuation amplitude
grasping force fluctuation percentage (~30% with jamming vs. ~2.5x higher without jamming)
successful grasping and transportation of diverse objects
possible_gap_implications: Placing stretchable jamming media on the non-contact dorsal surface provides an effective paradigm for decoupling tactile sensing/soft envelope adaptation from structural stiffening in soft actuators.
The occurrence of anisotropic bending moments points to an open mechanical modeling and design challenge in achieving uniform stiffness and curvature along multi-layered sliding structures.
paper.research_objective: To develop and experimentally evaluate a tensile Cross-Sliding jamming mechanism integrated on the upper surface of a soft bending actuator (and assemble a multi-fingered soft gripper) to remove assembly position restrictions, eliminate rigid contact with grasped objects, avoid contact surface disturbance during jamming, and achieve stable grasping with tunable stiffness.
paper.research_problem: Conventional variable stiffness structures for soft fingers lack stretchability and are therefore restricted to the lower/bending surface, causing rigid contact with objects during grasping, contact surface disturbances/fluctuations during jamming, and potential structural hollows/instabilities if stretched.
paper.title: A Soft Finger With Tensile Variable Stiffness Based on the Cross-Sliding Jamming Mechanism
